summary: TerraCrop AI turns NASA Earth observation data into simple, actionable crop decisions for farmers. Climate extremes, monoculture and complex satellite data leave smallholder farmers without usable guidance. Given a farm’s location, TerraCrop builds an environmental snapshot (temperature, rainfall anomaly, soil moisture, vegetation greenness) based on NASA POWER, SMAP and MODIS parameters. A deterministic optimizer using Multi-Attribute Utility Theory and agronomic rules (legume nitrogen breaks, no back-to-back Solanaceae) then creates a 1–5 year crop rotation plan that is reproducible and explainable. A Scenario Lab lets users test drought, flood and heatwave shocks. “Ask Terra”, a Gemini-powered voice and text assistant in English and Bangla, explains why each crop was chosen in plain language. To inspire the next generation, TerraFarm is a 2D pixel-art farming game where students till soil, plant crops and visit a NASA Earth Station to learn how SMAP, GPM and MODIS monitor farmland. Harvest choices carry over to the real planner.
details:
What it does: TerraCrop AI is a climate-aware crop rotation decision-support platform. A farmer enters or picks their farm location and gets a plain-language health card (soil water, weather and heat, crop greenness), a 1–5 year rotation plan, climate stress tests, a voice and text assistant, and a game that teaches the same concepts.

How it works:

  1. Environmental snapshot: temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, soil moisture, NDVI and a drought-risk index are built from NASA POWER, SMAP and MODIS-based parameters.
  2. Deterministic optimizer: crops are scored with Multi-Attribute Utility Theory across water, temperature, soil, season and farmer priority (Best Balanced, Save Water, Protect Soil). Botanical rules are enforced, such as penalties for continuous rice or potato and rewards for legume nitrogen fixation. Results are reproducible and explainable.
  3. Ask Terra (Google Gemini via @google/genai): the model only explains the optimizer’s results, grounded in the farm’s data, so it doesn’t invent recommendations. A rule-based fallback works without an API key.
  4. Scenario Lab: simulates -40% rainfall drought, +60% monsoon flood and +3°C to +5°C heatwaves to show which crops fail or survive.
  5. TerraFarm game (Phaser): a cozy pixel-art farm where players use a hoe, water can and seeds, pet farm animals, and visit a NASA Earth Station to learn about SMAP, GPM and MODIS. Crop choices transfer to the real planner.

Benefits and impact: Farmers understand their soil and weather risk in seconds. Rotation plans reduce fertilizer cost and protect soil and groundwater. Extension workers can test climate risks before advising communities. Students learn remote sensing and sustainable farming through play. The app is bilingual (English and Bangla) with text-to-speech to improve accessibility.

Tools: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Phaser, Leaflet, Node.js/Express, Supabase (auth and PostgreSQL with row-level security), Cloudflare Turnstile, Web Audio and Web Speech APIs, Google Gemini.

Creativity and factors considered: We combined an explainable deterministic engine with generative AI so advice is never hallucinated. We added a game to reach young people, offline-friendly cached baselines for poor connectivity, and bilingual voice support for rural users.

SI disclosure: Google Gemini is used at runtime in Ask Terra to explain results.
dataRefs: NASA POWER Agroclimatology (climate baseline for temperature, rainfall and solar radiation)
NASA SMAP – Soil Moisture Active Passive (soil moisture reference)
NASA MODIS Terra/Aqua NDVI, MOD13Q1 (vegetation greenness reference)
NASA GPM / IMERG (rainfall and flood-risk reference)
